newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow bounce boosts Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow bounce boosts Australian stocks at open.

text.p: Australian shares opened higher on Thursday with the market boosted by a Dow rebound after comments by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan comforted U.S. markets.
The All Ordinaries index added 20.0 points to 2,453.0.
Brokers said most sectors were showing gains although the gold sector softened with the weaker bullion price.

"It opened very strongly," said Jim Tredenick, senior dealer at Nevitts Ltd, although he cautioned that it was likely to ease as the day went on. "I wouldn't be surprised to see it drift off a bit later on," he said.

The big banks were the early leaders. The banking sector index was up 1.3 percent compared to a gain of about 0.9 percent in the benchmark All Ordinaries index. National Australia Bank, up 23 cents to A$16.46 (US$12.92) and Commonwealth Bank, up 24.3 cents to A$12.97 were the pick of the big four.
Golds, however, lost ground and the index was down 0.8 percent in early trade.
"Gold was a bit disappointing overseas last night and that has certainly brought the gold stocks down," Tredenick said.
Results continued apace with gas distributor AGL THE first cab off the rank. Its shares jumped 14 cents to A$7.50 after AGL reported a 19.6-percent higher half year net profit of A$75.6 million.

Paper and packaging giant Amcor lost five cents to A$8.44 after posting a sharply lower first-half net profit of A$140.6 million, while radio network operator Austereo was unchanged at A$2.25 in thin trade after its 11 percent higher first-half net profit of A$17.15 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to three, while about 36 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
